_meta.indication: Treatment of adults with community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (CABP) caused by susceptible microorganisms including S. pneumoniae, S. aureus (methicillin-susceptible), H. influenzae, L. pneumophila, M. pneumoniae, and C. pneumoniae.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-control, noninferiority trial of IV lefamulin 150 mg q12h with optional switch to oral 600 mg q12h versus IV moxifloxacin 400 mg q24h with optional oral switch.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with PORT III-V CABP
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percentage of subjects with Early Clinical Response (ECR) at 96 +/- 24 hours after the first dose of study drug in the ITT population
pivotal_trials.n: 551 (276 in LEF arm; 275 in MOX arm)
pivotal_trials.result: ECR rate was 87.3% for lefamulin and 90.2% for moxifloxacin, difference -2.9% (95% CI, -8.5% to 2.8%), meeting noninferiority.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-control, noninferiority trial of oral lefamulin 600 mg q12h for 5 days versus oral moxifloxacin 400 mg q24h for 7 days.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with PORT II-IV CABP
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percentage of subjects with Early Clinical Response (ECR) at 96 +/- 24 hours after the first dose of study drug in the ITT population
pivotal_trials.n: 738 (370 in LEF arm; 368 in MOX arm)
pivotal_trials.result: ECR rate was 90.8% for lefamulin and 90.8% for moxifloxacin, difference 0% (95% CI, -4.4% to 4.5%), meeting noninferiority.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥2%): for XENLETA Injection administration site reactions (7%), hepatic enzyme elevation, nausea, hypokalemia, insomnia, headache; for XENLETA Tablets diarrhea (12% vs 1% moxifloxacin), nausea (5%), vomiting (3%), hepatic enzyme elevation. Warnings include QT prolongation and embryo-fetal toxicity.
target_moa: Lefamulin is a pleuromutilin antibacterial that inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding the peptidyl transferase center (PTC) at the 50S subunit of the bacterial ribosome; mammalian protein synthesis appears unaffected.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held; applications were not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary.

summary.text: Lefamulin (XENLETA), a pleuromutilin antibacterial for CABP, was granted Fast Track and QIDP designation and Priority Review, and was approved as a standard (non-accelerated) approval based on two Phase 3 noninferiority trials.
